  "Then she put the hammer back exactly where she had found it."
  "Mr. Ruiz never learned who had fixed his porch."
]

  "To span wider rivers, the Romans built arch bridges out of curved stone."
  "The arch pushed the weight outward, so the bridge could carry heavy loads."
  "Later, engineers hung the roadway from cables in a suspension bridge."
  "Suspension bridges could cross gaps far too wide for any arch."
  "Each new design solved a problem the earlier one could not."
  "Today, engineers choose a design to fit the distance and the load."
]

target c1-t11 passage "How Bridges Changed" type informational lines [
  "Long ago, builders made bridges by laying flat stones across a stream."
  "These beam bridges could only cross short gaps before they sagged."
  "To span wider rivers, the Romans built arch bridges out of curved stone."
  "The arch pushed the weight outward, so the bridge could carry heavy loads."
  "Later, engineers hung the roadway from cables in a suspension bridge."
  "Suspension bridges could cross gaps far too wide for any arch."
  "Each new design solved a problem the earlier one could not."
  "Today, engineers choose a design to fit the distance and the load."
]

  claim id "c1" status supported dimension relationships-interactions subject "the bridge designs" standard ri-3 text "Each new bridge design fixed a problem the last one could not." cites ["e1" "e2" "e3"] {},

  claim id "c3" status distractor error-type erroneous-inference plausibility 0.6 targets ["q1" "q12"] text "The Romans invented every type of bridge in the article." rationale "Not stated; they built arch bridges, not all types." cites ["e5"] {},
  claim id "c4" status distractor error-type faulty-reasoning plausibility 0.6 targets ["q1" "q12"] text "Newer bridges are always prettier than older bridges." rationale "Beauty is never discussed; the text is about solving problems." cites ["e6"] {},
  claim id "c5" status distractor error-type misreads-detail plausibility 0.5 targets ["q1" "q12"] text "Suspension bridges are built only from curved stone." rationale "Confuses suspension bridges (cables) with arch bridges (stone)." cites ["e7"] {},
  claim id "c6" status distractor error-type erroneous-inference plausibility 0.5 targets ["q1" "q12"] text "Engineers today still prefer the simple beam bridge." rationale "Contradicted; they choose a design by distance and load." cites ["e8"] {}
]

A tiny crab scuttled under a rock, and Mara smiled for the first time all day.
She traced the cold water as if the pool were the only thing that mattered.
Five more minutes, she whispered, though no one was listening.
Behind her, paper plates rustled and her mother laughed.
The waves pushed a ribbon of seaweed against her fingers.
Her sandwich sat untouched on the blanket by the cooler.
Mara cares more about the tide pool than the picnic.
Mara is angry at her brother for calling her.
Her silence is absorption, not anger.
Mara does not like being outdoors at the beach.
Contradicted by her smile at the crab.
Mara is afraid of her own family at the beach.
Her quiet whisper is treated as fear without support.
Mara is bored by the quiet water of the tide pool.
Her stillness shows focus, not boredom.
Mara wants to leave the beach and go home.
Nothing shows a wish to leave; she asks for more time.

  "The queen lays the eggs that become the colony's next generation."

  "Honeybees live together in large groups called colonies."
  "Every bee in the colony has a job that helps the whole group survive."
  "Worker bees gather nectar, build the honeycomb, and feed the young."
  "Guard bees stand at the entrance and protect the hive from intruders."
  "The queen lays the eggs that become the colony's next generation."
  "When a worker finds flowers, it dances to tell the others where to go."
  "In winter, the bees cluster together and beat their wings to stay warm."
  "Because each bee does its part, the colony can do things no single bee could do alone."
]

A tiny crab scuttled under a rock, and Mara smiled for the first time all day.
She traced the cold water as if the pool were the only thing that mattered.
Five more minutes, she whispered, though no one was listening.
Behind her, paper plates rustled and her mother laughed.
Mara cares more about the tide pool than the picnic.
Mara is angry at her brother.
Mara is upset with her family.
Which of these inferences about Mara is supported by the passage?
Which sentence(s) from the passage best support your answer in Part A?
